games.title: Arx Fatalis
games.note: Arkane's first game; spells are cast by drawing runes with the mouse in an underground world.

games.title: Dark Messiah of Might and Magic
games.note: Built on Valve's Source engine; players remember kicking enemies off ledges and into spike racks.

games.title: Prey (2017)
games.note: Shares only a name with the 2006 Prey; its alien Mimics disguise themselves as everyday objects.

games.title: Deathloop
games.note: One day on the island of Blackreef repeats until you take down eight targets within a single loop.

games.title: Weird West
games.note: Raphaël Colantonio's first game after leaving Arkane: a top-down immersive sim in a supernatural Wild West.

games.title: Thief: Deadly Shadows
games.note: Made by Ion Storm Austin after Looking Glass closed; its Shalebridge Cradle level is famous as a horror set piece.

games.title: Deus Ex: Invisible War
games.note: Directed by Harvey Smith and built for PC and Xbox at once; all weapons share a single ammo type.

games.title: Deus Ex: Mankind Divided
games.note: Set two years after Human Revolution, mostly in a near-future Prague where augmented people are segregated.

games.title: System Shock (2023)
games.note: Nightdive's remake took seven and a half years, restarting twice before its May 2023 release.

games.title: Underworld Ascendant
games.note: Paul Neurath's Kickstarter-funded return to the Stygian Abyss; it was poorly received at launch.

games.title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell
games.note: Began as a sci-fi spy project called The Drift; Sam Fisher's glowing night-vision goggles became its trademark.

games.title: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Chaos Theory
games.note: Clint Hocking was creative director; it added a two-player co-op campaign.

games.title: Mark of the Ninja
games.note: Shows the noise you make as visible rings, so a 2D game can play like a stealth sim.

games.title: Silent Service
games.note: Sid Meier's World War II submarine simulation, where staying hidden is your best defense.

games.title: GoldenEye 007
games.note: Higher difficulty settings add extra mission objectives, not just tougher enemies.

games.title: Suikoden
games.note: You recruit 108 characters, a nod to the classic Chinese novel Water Margin.

links.took: Looking Glass's Underworld engine, ported and extended, and its simulation-driven play.
links.added: A sci-fi space station, a villainous AI called SHODAN and story told through logs.
links.extra: Doug Church, a lead on Underworld, directed System Shock, with Warren Spector producing.

links.took: The emergent play and immersive spaces of both Underworld games.
links.added: Streamlined them into one 'integrated whole', with logs and emails instead of conversations.

links.took: Looking Glass's team, including Doug Church, and its simulation-first design.
links.added: Stealth built on light, shadow and sound, in a city of thieves and rival factions.

links.took: Sneaking past guards in a castle; it was one of Ken Levine's favorite games.
links.added: First-person stealth where light and sound decide whether you are seen.

src.t: Wikipedia: Thief: The Dark Project (cites Ken Levine)

links.took: Not specified; Ken Levine named Diablo among the favorite games that inspired the project.
links.added: Not specified in the source.

src.t: Wikipedia: Thief: The Dark Project (cites Ken Levine)

links.took: Submarine warfare's logic: powerful while hidden, vulnerable once detected.
links.added: Applied that logic to a medieval thief moving through shadows.

src.t: Wikipedia: Thief: The Dark Project (cites Ken Levine)

links.extra: Levine traced the stealth concept to submarine warfare and Silent Service.

links.took: Difficulty levels that change mission objectives, not just enemy strength.
links.added: Harder settings add rules such as not killing anyone.

links.took: Thief's Dark Engine; the two games shared most of their code during development.
links.added: RPG skills, psionic powers and survival horror aboard a starship.
links.extra: Ken Levine, Thief's original designer, led System Shock 2's design at Irrational Games.

links.took: The immersive-sim foundations Warren Spector said he wanted to build on.
links.added: A near-future conspiracy story with several ways to finish every mission.
links.extra: Spector produced System Shock at Looking Glass before leading Ion Storm's Austin studio.

links.took: Stealth as a real alternative to fighting; Spector's design document cited Thief.
links.added: Combined stealth with hacking, conversation and body augmentations.

src.t: Wikipedia: Deus Ex (cites Warren Spector's design document)

links.took: Named in Spector's original design document as a gameplay inspiration.
links.added: RPG skills and several paths through each level instead of one scripted route.

src.t: Wikipedia: Deus Ex (cites Warren Spector's design document)

links.took: RPG choices and consequences, cited in Spector's design document.
links.added: First-person play that blends shooter, stealth and role-playing.

src.t: Wikipedia: Deus Ex (cites Warren Spector's design document)

links.took: Named in Spector's design document as a gameplay inspiration.
links.added: Not specified in the source.

src.t: Wikipedia: Deus Ex (cites Warren Spector's design document)

links.took: Spector cited the limited choices in the first Suikoden as an inspiration.
links.added: A much broader range of story and gameplay choices.

links.took: A 1978 D&D session with Bruce Sterling, whose story grew from the players' choices.
links.added: Tried to recreate that player-driven storytelling in a computer game.

links.took: Augmentations, conspiracies and multiple solutions to every mission.
links.added: A story set 20 years later, built for both PC and Xbox, with universal ammo.

links.took: Garrett, the City and light-and-shadow stealth.
links.added: Free roaming through the City between missions, and an optional third-person view.

links.took: Ion Storm Austin's team and the technology it built for Invisible War.
links.added: Applied it to Thief's light-and-shadow stealth.
links.extra: Ion Storm Austin made both after Looking Glass Studios closed in 2000.

links.took: Adam Jensen, augmentations and the hub-based level structure.
links.added: A divided society that segregates augmented people, centered on Prague.

links.took: System Shock 2's mechanics, which shaped plasmids, weapon upgrades and stealth.
links.added: An underwater city built on Ayn Rand's ideas, and the 'Would you kindly' twist.
links.extra: Irrational Games and Ken Levine made both; BioShock is widely called a spiritual successor to System Shock.

links.took: Player-powered play, which Ken Levine called 'the spirit of System Shock'.
links.added: A retro-futuristic city under the sea and a moral choice over the Little Sisters.

links.took: Levine said all the games he worked on came from inspiration he took from Underworld.
links.added: Plasmid powers, environmental storytelling and a strong central narrative.

links.took: Exploring a 3D underground world; Toby Gard said he was 'a big fan' of Underworld.
links.added: A third-person polygon heroine, acrobatics and puzzle-filled tombs.
links.extra: Gard wanted to combine that style of game with polygon characters.

links.took: Not specified; Cliff Bleszinski said Underworld had 'far more impact on me than Doom'.
links.added: Not specified in the source.

links.took: Underworld's first-person dungeon RPG; Arkane first pitched a third Ultima Underworld.
links.added: Spells cast by drawing runes, and a whole society living underground.

src.t: Wikipedia: Ultima Underworld: The Stygian Abyss

links.extra: After Electronic Arts turned the pitch down, Arkane made Arx Fatalis as a spiritual successor.

links.took: Paul Neurath and the Stygian Abyss setting.
links.added: A Kickstarter-funded return built around improvising with physics and magic.

links.took: The immersive first-person design that Underworld pioneered.
links.added: Physics puzzles, the gravity gun and a city-wide story told without cutscenes.

src.t: Wikipedia: Ultima Underworld: The Stygian Abyss

links.extra: Wikipedia lists Half-Life 2 among games influenced by Underworld but quotes no one.

links.took: Arkane's first-person fantasy combat and physics-based interaction.
links.added: Valve's Source engine, kicking enemies into traps and a Might and Magic setting.

src.t: Wikipedia: Dark Messiah of Might and Magic

links.took: Arkane's first-person melee, magic and physics systems.
links.added: Stealth, supernatural powers and a plague-ridden city with many routes.

src.t: Wikipedia: Dark Messiah of Might and Magic

links.extra: Both are Arkane games; Raphaël Colantonio co-directed Dishonored with Harvey Smith.

links.took: Thief's light-and-shadow stealth; Colantonio said Dishonored grew out of a Thief 4 pitch.
links.added: Powers such as Blink and a city inspired by plague-era London.

src.t: Raphaël Colantonio and Harvey Smith, via PC Gamer, 2026

links.extra: Wikipedia says Dishonored's stealth system was originally based on Thief's.

links.took: Harvey Smith and Ricardo Bare from Deus Ex, and missions with many solutions.
links.added: A whale-oil-powered city, supernatural powers and a chaos system that tracks how lethal you are.

links.took: BioShock-style world design, as Kotaku's review put it.
links.added: Deus Ex-style freedom in each mission, plus supernatural powers.

src.t: Wikipedia: Dishonored (cites Jason Schreier's Kotaku review)

links.took: Visual design director Viktor Antonov, who designed Half-Life 2's City 17.
links.added: Dunwall, an industrial city drawn from London and Edinburgh.

links.took: System Shock's mood and enclosed-station structure; Colantonio called it a key influence.
links.added: Mimics that hide as objects, a foam-shooting GLOO cannon and powers taken from aliens.
links.extra: Colantonio said Dishonored followed Thief, while Prey aimed for a System Shock-like enclosed experience.

links.took: Arkane's immersive-sim systems; Colantonio said Prey was less stealth-focused than Dishonored.
links.added: A role-playing upgrade system of Neuromods and chipsets on a space station.

links.took: The interconnected 'mega-dungeon' idea from Arkane's Arx Fatalis.
links.added: Turned it into the space station Talos I, open to explore in any order.

links.took: The D&D Mimic, a monster disguised as an ordinary object.
links.added: Alien Mimics that can copy any object on a space station.
links.extra: Wikipedia lists the D&D Mimic among Prey's influences without naming who said so.

links.took: Dishonored's powers and level design; director Dinga Bakaba called it 'Dishonored with guns'.
links.added: A time loop on one island where you learn routines to take down eight targets.

links.took: Arkane's roguelike experiment in Prey: Mooncrash, which remixed limited spaces.
links.added: A loop structure with an invading rival, Julianna, whom another player can control.

links.took: Arkane Lyon's team and the Dishonored universe, which Deathloop shares.
links.added: Guns, a 1960s-style island and a day that resets.

links.took: Raphaël Colantonio and Arkane's immersive-sim design.
links.added: A top-down supernatural Western with five linked character stories.
links.extra: Colantonio founded WolfEye with former Arkane executive producer Julien Roby.

links.took: The top-down view of the early Fallout games.
links.added: Real-time systemic play where fire, water and electricity interact.
links.extra: Wikipedia says the perspective was inspired by early Ultima and Fallout games.

links.took: Citadel Station, SHODAN and the original 1994 level layouts.
links.added: Rebuilt in Unreal Engine with modern controls and graphics.

links.took: Third-person stealth action; producer Mathieu Ferland called MGS 'a huge inspiration'.
links.added: Light meters, night vision and gadgets grounded in real spycraft.

src.t: Wikipedia: Splinter Cell (cites Mathieu Ferland and Clint Hocking)

links.extra: Designer Clint Hocking said the game owes its existence to the Metal Gear series.

links.took: Ubisoft set out to make a 'Metal Gear Solid 2 killer'.
links.added: A darker, more realistic take on sneaking, built around light and shadow.

links.took: Light-and-shadow stealth; designer Clint Hocking cited Thief as an influence.
links.added: Third-person acrobatics and modern spy gadgets.

links.took: Cited by designer Clint Hocking as an influence, alongside System Shock and Thief.
links.added: A focused stealth game built around a single spy.

links.took: Sam Fisher and light-based stealth.
links.added: More open levels, a knife for close combat and two-player co-op.

src.t: Wikipedia: Tom Clancy's Splinter Cell: Chaos Theory

links.took: Stealth built on light and noise, which Thief popularized.
links.added: A 2D side view that draws sound and sight lines on screen.
links.extra: Genre link only. Lead designer Nels Anderson said his spark was the lack of stealthy ninjas in games like Ninja Gaiden.

links.took: Stealth as the core of play; Thief's influence is recognized in later stealth games.
links.added: Disguises and contract killings in open-ended levels.
links.extra: Wikipedia, citing GamePro, names Hitman, Splinter Cell and Assassin's Creed among stealth games Thief influenced.

links.took: Stealth as the core of play, part of Thief's recognized influence.
links.added: Blending into crowds, free-running and open historical cities.
